newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek seamen block ships, call 24-hr strike Friday.
newsitem.headline: Greek seamen block ships, call 24-hr strike Friday.

text.p: Greek seamen set a new 24-hour strike for Friday after stopping many ships from docking and clashing with police at several ports on Thursday.
The Panhellenic Seamen's Federation (PNO) said it extended the strike begun on Monday to protest against unemployment and the abolition of special tax exemptions.
They are also demanding changes in insurance and pension programmes.
The new strike was decided after PNO's unsuccessful meeting with merchant marine minister Stavros Soumakis on 19 December to discuss the seamen's demands.
There were clashes again at Piraeus, near Athens, and Patras and Igoumenitsa in western Greece on Thursday, police said.
Seaman have been trying to stop ships from docking, often by diving into the sea in front of the pier. They have also fought with lorry drivers trying to unload goods.

The clashes on Wednesday and Thursday have involved both police trying to keep seamen away from ships and lorry drivers, and fights between seamen and lorry drivers. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
